text.p: Swiss inspection and testing group Societe Generale de Surveillance Holdings SA said on Monday that net profit after taxes, minority interests and goodwill amortisation rose to 262.7 million Swiss francs in 1996 from 230.4 million in 1995, a 14 percent increase.
It also said that it would propose an increase in its dividend paid on registered and bearer shares.
The dividend paid on registered shares would be increased to 13.20 francs per share from 11.20 francs.
The dividend paid on bearer shares would be increased to 66.00 francs from 56.00 francs, it said.
Surveillance said that its consolidated revenues totalled 2.954 billion francs, an increase of 12.4 percent from 2.628 billion in 1995.
In local currencies, revenues increased by 10.7 percent, it said.
It said that internal growth contributed 9.3 percent to the overall increase, while acquisitions accounted for 1.4 percent.

"The positive currency translation impact on the group's revenues was 1.7 percent due to the weakening of the Swiss franc against the U.S. dollar and most European currencies," it said. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
